title: Routing Tests and Troubleshooting knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Routing Tests and Troubleshooting”?
options: Routing Tests and Troubleshooting helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Routing Tests and Troubleshooting means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Routing Tests and Troubleshooting removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Routing Tests and Troubleshooting should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Routing Tests and Troubleshooting helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Routing Tests and Troubleshooting is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Testing route configuration” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Testing route configuration” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Testing route configuration” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Testing route configuration” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Testing route configuration” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Testing route configuration” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Testing route configuration” under Routing Tests and Troubleshooting. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Routing Tests and Troubleshooting”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
